features.note: Continuous daylight runs under the whole leading half of the leaf in both the hero and the grazing views, and the opening carries no track and the leading edge no wheel. In the abierto capture the opening is completely empty except the catch post — which is the clearest possible statement that nothing crosses the road.

MEASURED, not assumed. In the hero view the mesh behind the tail could have been either the fence or a filled counterbalance; the CERCA-off capture settles it — with the fence hidden the tail is a bare braced frame with its two diagonals and no infill whatsoever. The 50% proportion is legible in the abierto view, where 2.50 m of open frame sits against a 5.00 m clear opening.

Two carriages under the tail with their rollers on the rail, and the concrete beam continues well past the parked leaf — visibly longer than the opening, which is the point. The beam reads brighter than intended (see defects).

Does NOT collapse to flat grey or to black, which is the documented failure for bare metal on a vertical subject. Measured on the top rail: [86,92,99] near the leading edge, [78,84,90] mid-leaf, [62,67,71] over the tail — a smooth fall-off, i.e. a lit metal surface rather than a flat fill. dE00 0.03 against the declared anchor.

Lowest critical feature, and honestly so. The receiving fork on the catch post and the guide-roller head on the gate post are both present and correctly placed, but each is a ~0.2 m detail on a 12.6 m subject: they read at the grazing scale, not at the hero scale.

important_features.note: The fence line sits behind the tail and explains why the tail is unfilled. Moving the camera to the approach side was what made this readable — from the fence side the fence occluded the very thing it was there to justify.

The gear motor reads clearly as a yellow housing beside the first carriage. The module-4 rack is at true pitch (12.57 mm), so at hero scale its teeth are sub-pixel and it reads as a dark strip; correct, but it carries no detail until the grazing view.

defects: The hero camera cannot frame both states: it is framed on the leaf and its posts (7.60 m), so in the OPEN state the parked leaf runs off the right edge. This was caught by the pre-look and answered with a dedicated `abierto` view framed on the full 12.60 m travel envelope — but it means the DEFAULT camera alone is not sufficient evidence for this asset, which is a property of the subject, not a bug.

The concrete foundation beam renders as the brightest object in the frame: it is a broad horizontal face taking the key almost head-on, and it pulls the eye to the ground strip rather than to the gate.
The module-4 drive rack is at true pitch, so its teeth are sub-pixel at hero scale and it reads as a plain dark strip. Faithful, but it contributes nothing to the hero read.
In the abierto view the catch post sits at the very left edge (ndcX -0.879). It is inside the frame, but with almost no margin.

mechanical.note: Console-clean read from all THREE capture sidecars (?view=neutral, ?view=grazing, ?view=abierto), each console_clean:true with an empty issues array. probe.mjs medians 41 draws / 13,738 tris against a budget of 60 / 200,000; fps ignored (informational under SwiftShader). No test suite for this design, so tests is null rather than fabricated. Preflight PASS including distinctness on both pairs (neutral vs abierto, grazing vs abierto). DEVIATIONS, recorded rather than hidden: (1) the reviewer is the ORCHESTRATOR INLINE, not a fresh-context blind agent — this session cannot spawn subagents, so this verdict is a SELF-REVIEW and not the independent acceptance authority GATES.md requires; jaula-seguridad's inline verdict was subsequently confirmed by a real blind reviewer, but that is evidence about one asset, not a licence for this one. (2) The `neutral` evidence view is deliberately the default camera. (3) No `reference-match` view: no reference photographs exist (p6_comparison: spec-only). TWO PRE-LOOK CORRECTIONS were applied before this review was written: the camera was on the FENCE side, so the fence occluded the counterbalance; and the NDC framing criterion was maximising a bbox rectangle, which rewards a steep diagonal — a long thin subject seen end-on scored 61% while reading as a fence receding to the horizon. Both were invisible to every mechanical check, which is the same class of blindness the framing check itself was written to cover.
